document: remediation amendment to protocol.json after the independent review of increment 9
status: post-measurement remediation: written after every increment-9 measurement and after the independent review; revised after the second independent review (R10 added, R5-R7 relabelled). R1-R9 tighten the acceptance gate or add preconditions; R10 is not a tightening: it corrects the semantics of the preservation rule after measurement. No approved numerical threshold is changed
protocol_json_untouched: protocol.json is byte-identical to the committed file; the gate pins its SHA256 and reads both files
review_limit: the review could not verify the content of protocol.json before the 14:56:31Z amendment, because that amendment was written in place; only the amended text is in Git

unchanged.stock_fp64_diagnostic: raw verdict FAIL kept and reported; never rewritten to PASS

changes.before: a condition could be PASS with an evidence file missing, empty or reduced to its derived boolean
changes.after: a missing file or field is NOT PROVEN, a contradicted fact is FAIL; 'passed', 'all_match' and similar derived booleans are recomputed from raw per-file, per-phase and per-tensor records

changes.before: only stock_fp32 and full64 reports were required
changes.after: the stock_fp64 diagnostic report is mandatory evidence: if missing F is NOT PROVEN; its raw FAIL does not fail F and is reported unchanged; a report whose recorded verdict differs from its own comparisons is FAIL

parity reports must name the phase-B runtime report, revision, sequence, contract, dtype, profile, approved thresholds and complete element counts (8x152064 logits, 28x8x3584 residuals, KV prefix per phase); the worker's scope unit and output file must be the supervisor's; runtime source SHA256 must equal the official LFS digests of the preflight; per-tensor read counters must equal the official header shapes times the positions; gate 7, gate 8 and the git preservation are recomputed by their own tools; capture files are re-hashed when present locally

changes.before: fact 'streaming SHA equals LFS' compared the copied official digest with itself
changes.after: proof is post-acquisition only: full SHA256 computed by the runtime at the start of both phase-B runs and the recorded re-hash, each compared per file with the official LFS digests of the preflight, over the complete file set (4 shards, index, SmolLM2 model). The acquisition-time check of the historical run is stated as a limitation: the code raised on mismatch, the computed digest was not recorded

changes.area: phase B eviction and reads (conditions C, D, G)
changes.after: for both phaseB-sync and phaseB-pipeline: condition 'evicted'; residency after eviction <= 1% of each shard, shard set equal to the four shards and sizes equal to the hashed files; inference block reads >= 90% of logical inference bytes
changes.chosen_after_measurement: the 1% residency limit (resident_after_eviction_max_fraction 0.01) and the 90% block-read fraction (phase_b_block_read_min_fraction 0.9) are new thresholds, not preregistered, chosen after the measured values were known (residency 0 B; block reads 99.4% of logical bytes in sync)

changes.before: memory.peak <= memory.max (true by kernel enforcement) with oom/oom_kill = 0 and swap 0; anonymous+kernel charge 'well below the limit', reported only
changes.after: in addition, for every supervised run: sampled peak of memory.stat anon + kernel <= 268435456 B and worker VmHWM <= 268435456 B (the RLIMIT_AS of the worker, 12.5% of memory.max)
changes.limit_of_evidence: anon and kernel are sampled every 50 ms and can miss transients; VmHWM is the kernel high-water mark but is bounded by RLIMIT_AS anyway
changes.informative_part: the worker VmHWM limit adds nothing: it is implied by RLIMIT_AS = 268435456 B (256 MiB) of the worker, since resident memory cannot exceed the address space. Only the anon + kernel limit is informative: measured maximum 110895104 B, margin about 2.4x, on values sampled every 50 ms

changes.before: substring tests on the last line of pytest and unittest outputs
changes.after: pytest: only dotted progress lines followed by exactly 'N passed in Ts' with N >= minimum_pytest_passed (613: the 484 tests of the original increment plus 129 review regressions); unittest: 'Ran N tests' with N at least the expected count and last line exactly 'OK'; the oracle 8 and precision 7 check outputs are now required
changes.chosen_after_measurement: the minimum counts (613 pytest tests; 3, 1 and 5 unittest tests) are the counts observed when the remediation was written, not preregistered values; minimum_pytest_passed stays 613 although later follow-ups add tests

changes.before: supervisor and audit files contained the absolute path of the local checkout, a session scratch path, a terminal-session identifier and one Hugging Face cache entry unrelated to the project
changes.after: these strings are replaced by placeholders or dropped by declared mechanical rules (sanitization-manifest.json); no number is changed; originals stay local in a git-ignored directory. New gate precondition: every sanitized file must equal the digest in the manifest and, when the originals are present, must be exactly its original under the declared rules; otherwise every condition is FAIL (or NOT PROVEN if the manifest is missing). Second review: the gate pins the names and the original and sanitized SHA256 of the eleven sanitized files; an empty manifest, a removed entry or a local original not listed in the manifest is FAIL

changes.before: protocol.json was read but not checked
changes.after: precondition: protocol.json must have the committed SHA256, the approved thresholds and limits, and this amendment must carry exactly the gate parameters; otherwise every condition is FAIL (or NOT PROVEN if a file is missing)

changes.before: every path returned by 'git diff --name-only <baseline>' counted as modified and had to be in the intentional list; files added by the increment were invisible only while they were untracked
changes.after: only files that existed at the baseline are judged (modified or type-changed, and deleted); files added after the baseline are listed separately (added_since_baseline, new_untracked) and are not judged
changes.why: once the increment was committed the original rule failed on every file the increment itself added; the rule was changed after that was observed, which makes H pass
changes.limit: files added by increment 9 (for example inwime_runtime/qwen2.py and the increment-9 tools and tests) are not protected by the preservation check; git flags such as --assume-unchanged or --skip-worktree are not detected
changes.kind: not a tightening: semantic correction made after measurement
